h: Torah Guides Our Steps and Reveals the Purpose of Suffering

p: (רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה לה, א)
(at the beginning of this parsha, Vayikra Rabbah 35:1):
"'If you will walk in My statutes'
and turned my feet back to Your testimonies.'
'I am going to such-and-such a place, etc.,'
and my feet would bring me
to the batei knesios and the batei midrash, etc."
Now this needs to be understood:
that it was so every single day?
Perhaps it happened to him so
But it appears that they inferred it precisely
"Only goodness and kindness shall pursue me
all the days of my life" — precisely so.
for "good" means nothing other than Torah
and "kindness" is also words of Torah,
for when his feet would lead him
he would teach Torah to the many,
"He who sits in the seat of wisdom,"
and Torah studied in order to teach it
all the days of my life,"
meaning that my feet lead me
to the beis midrash every day.
This is along the lines of what they said
and in the Mechilta (end of Parshas Yisro)
and in Avos d'Rabbi Nosson (end of chapter 12)
"To the place that my heart loves,
that my heart is bound up with the words of Torah.
For David was the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
(בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ, א)
(in the Midrash Rabbah at the beginning of Parshas Acharei, Vayikra Rabbah 20:1):
"Whoever saw him was reminded of his learning";
He said this in the language of prayer:
אָמַר דָּוִד רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי
"David said: Master of the world, etc.,"
after this blemish had been written about him;
he said that his heart was bound up with Hashem Yisbarach,
along the lines of the derashah (Berachos 11a):
it is in your own going that you are obligated";
"I turned my feet back to Your testimonies"
And the blemish that was written
he merited the words of Torah,
And so too, "If you will walk in My statutes":
it is written simply "you will walk,"
and walking for a mitzvah is not mentioned,
as in "Fortunate are those whose way is perfect,
who walk in the Torah of Hashem" (Tehillim 119:1);
so it speaks of plain walking, your own.
that the words of Torah be engraved in the heart
will be to the words of Torah,
And just above it is written (Tehillim 119:58):
"I entreated Your presence with all my heart"
"be gracious to me according to Your word."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רלד, ב)
"And you shall say in your heart";
and that is Torah she'b'al peh,
which is "my word shall flow like dew" (Devarim 32:2).
"If you will walk in My statutes."
it is worse than if he had not learned,
as the Midrash Rabbah reckons it
"It would be better for him, etc."
the day when "Hashem gives you rest
from your sorrow and your agitation, etc." (Yeshayahu 14:3)
which is the sorrow and agitation
for Shabbos is a time of Torah,
when the words of Torah are engraved in the heart,
so that it becomes "you will walk";
and this mizmor is recited on Shabbos.

p: I considered what You wrote for us,
'If you will walk in My statutes,'
'And I will grant peace in the land' (Vayikra 26:6);
and 'if you will not listen to Me' (Vayikra 26:14),
why did he mention these particular pesukim?
regarding the question of the Rishonim:
of the reward of Olam Haba
is better than all the life of this world"
(as they said in the fourth chapter of Avos, 4:17);
and likewise, all of Iyov's sufferings
against one moment of the punishment of Gehinnom
(as the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote).
to tell us of reward and punishment,
for the purpose of avodah is
שֶׁתִּהְיֶה שֶׁלֹּא עַל מְנָת לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס
that it be not for the sake of receiving a reward
(as they said in the first chapter of Avos, 1:3).
Rather, what is mentioned in this parsha is
that if "you will walk in My statutes,"
in all the matters of this world
that help a person in the service of Hashem Yisbarach;
and likewise, in the opposite case,
in order to bring them back in teshuvah
And this is what is meant
what is said, "If you will walk in My statutes,"
"And I will grant peace in the land."
For this is the main intent
namely, that the eating be in holiness,
"I will grant peace in the land,"
from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
for this is the essence of peace;
as it says of the opposite, chas v'shalom
"There is no peace in my bones
He makes even his enemies at peace with him' (Mishlei 16:7)
this is the yetzer hara, etc.";
"and He will make it at peace with you."
And in the opposite case, chas v'shalom,
for this is the first time
to be the opposite of good
כַּאֲשֶׁר יְיַסֵּר אִישׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ וְגוֹ׳
"as a man chastises his son, etc." (Devarim 8:5);
"He who spares his rod hates his son,
but he who loves him chastises him early."
the Midrash Rabbah on Shemos opens (Shemos Rabbah 1:1),
for the entire exile of Egypt
as stated in the holy Zohar
the day when "Hashem gives you rest
from your sorrow and your agitation, etc.,"
that everything that seems the opposite
the eating on Shabbos is in holiness,
"I will give your rains in their season, etc." (Vayikra 26:4):
for Hashem Yisbarach is the Giver,
and from Him nothing but good comes forth;
from the accusation of the yetzer hara;
as they said in the Mechilta
"'Who keeps Shabbos from profaning it, etc.' (Yeshayahu 56:2)"
that he is guarded from sin.
"and you shall lie down with none to make you afraid" (Vayikra 26:6).

rich.text: “ואלה שמות בני ישראל הבאים מצרימה את יעקב איש וביתו באו, הדא הוא דכתיב (משלי יג, כד): חושך שבטו שונא בנו ואהבו שחרו מוסר, בנהג שבעולם אדם שאומר לו חברו …”

— ““These are the names of the children of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob; each came with his household” (Exodus 1:1). That is what is written: “He who spares his rod hates his son, and he who loves him …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Vayikra 26:6 — “ונתתי שלום בארץ ושכבתם ואין מחריד והשבתי חיה רעה מן הארץ וחרב לא תעבר בארצכם” — “I will grant peace in the land, and you shall lie down untroubled by anyone; I will give the land respite from vicious beasts, and no sword shall cross your land.”

rich.text: “ונתתי שלום בארץ ושכבתם ואין מחריד והשבתי חיה רעה מן הארץ וחרב לא תעבר בארצכם”
— “I will grant peace in the land, and you shall lie down untroubled by anyone; I will give the land respite from vicious beasts, and no sword shall cross your land.”
